open_points.subject: runner_source
open_points.text: On os.fork and on starting a thread the audit hook MUST count the tasks by listing the task directory of every process the environment's proc lists, opening no file there — an open outside the exchange directory and the readable_paths is itself a trap hit —, and, when the new task would exceed process_count, write a resource hit to the channel and raise, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; a creation the outer limit refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).
open_points.other_text: runner_source: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST return the text of one self-contained Python program for the release interpreter that imports only the standard library and nothing of the kernel's package; the program takes every fact of one execution from its command line as runner_arguments builds it, so the text is the same for every execution and holds no list, bound, path or descriptor number of its own.
open_points.question: Must the program be allowed to hold the proc filesystem path needed to list its processes and task directories, or must runner_arguments provide that path in the configuration?
